headline: Netanyahu bloc 54, Eisenkot bloc 50, NEITHER reaches 61 without Arab parties
dek: The Arab vote may decide Oct 27: with Netanyahu's bloc ~51-54 and the Jewish opposition ~50-55, the 13-15 Arab seats are the kingmaker. Eisenkot leads Netanyahu 45-33 as preferred PM (Channel 12, gap widened from 10 to 12 pts).
sources: Channel 12 survey (n=507, MoE 4.4%); KAN poll; Stat-Net Research Institute; Anadolu Agency; Turkiye Today; Reuters polling averages (via blogspot piece — treat the piece as low-cred, the cited polls as attributed)
fault_line: Will a record Arab turnout decide Netanyahu's fate — and would either Jewish bloc actually govern with Arab parties to reach 61?

sections.what_happened: The Arab vote may decide Oct 27: with Netanyahu's bloc ~51-54 and the Jewish opposition ~50-55, the 13-15 Arab seats are the kingmaker. Eisenkot leads Netanyahu 45-33 as preferred PM (Channel 12, gap widened from 10 to 12 pts). Arab turnout projected at 63% (Stat-Net) up to 70% (Tibi). Turnout enthusiasm favors the opposition (81% vs 74%).
sections.what_verified: AA, Turkiye Today, europesays, TRT World (Oct 11 wave), JPost (Oct 16 Maariv wave) agree on the arithmetic and the Eisenkot lead. The blogspot piece aggregates Reuters-cited polls — usable only for the poll citations, not as a source itself.
sections.what_disputed: Pollster divergence (Filber: right-wing majority — flagged at 05:00). Whether Arab parties would join ANY coalition remains uncertain (all outlets note it). Turnout projections are projections, not votes.
sections.why_matters: The kingmaker nobody counted: Arab-vote arithmetic map — 54 vs 50 vs 13-15. The election is 6 days out; Trump's endorsement failing to move the needle is the engagement hook (debate-bait: does a US president's endorsement help or hurt in Israel?).
sections.context: Background: Israel election Oct 27 — UPDATE: new kingmaker fault line — Stat-Net projects 63% Arab turnout; Kan poll: ~70% Arab turnout would deliver 13-15 Arab seats (up from 10); Reuters polling averages: Netanyahu bloc 54, Eisenkot bloc 50, NEITHER reaches 61 without Arab parties; Channel 12 (Oct 20): Eisenkot 45 vs Netanyahu 33 as preferred PM, Yashar 24 vs Likud 21; Trump's endorsement 'did not translate into more votes' (Turkiye Today); Joint List leader Ahmad Tibi predicts up to 70% turnout

totw_analysis: Our read: The kingmaker nobody counted: Arab-vote arithmetic map — 54 vs 50 vs 13-15. The election is 6 days out; Trump's endorsement failing to move the needle is the engagement hook (debate-bait: does a US president's endorsement help or hurt in Israel?). The fault line our audience is arguing over: Will a record Arab turnout decide Netanyahu's fate — and would either Jewish bloc actually govern with Arab parties to reach 61?
